1 غَمَتَهُ , aor.
غَمِتَ , (S, O, K,) inf. n. غَمْتٌ, (S, O,) It (i. e. food) was, or became, heavy upon his heart [or stomach], (Ks, S, O, K,) he having eaten much thereof so that it caused him to suffer indigestion, (Ks, O,) and it rendered him like one intoxicated: (K:) or, accord. to Sh, it (i. e. grease) rendered him like one intoxicated, (O, TA,) in consequence of indigestion. (TA.) ―
-b2- And He covered it; (O, K;) namely, a thing. (K.) ―
-b3- And غَمَتَهُ فِى المَآءِ i. q. غَطَّهُ [i. e. He immersed, or plunged, him, or it, into the water; like غَتَّهُ]. (IDrd, O, K.) ―
-b4- And غَمَتَ نَفَسًا He made a sign, or motion, with' his head, (O,) or he raised his head, (K,) [for the purpose of taking breath,] in drinking. (O, K.) ＝
-A2- غَمِتَ He became like one intoxicated, by grease [in his stomach]: (Sh, O:) or he suffered from the heaviness of food upon his heart [or stomach] so that he became like one intoxicated. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
